new_destinations.name: Dandenong Ranges
new_destinations.coordinates_source: centroid of kept spots (planning point, provisional); re-centre when spot pins are resolved
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage region page "Dandenong Ranges" (see Belgrave, Olinda, Sassafras); Visit Yarra Valley and Dandenong Ranges tourism brand; Puffing Billy headline attraction.
new_destinations.reason: 15 kept spots. The region is the named destination; the national park is a spot of it (the park and region are not separate pins). Melbourne region does not own these: Montsalvat/Eltham stays standalone.

new_destinations.name: Yarra Valley
new_destinations.coordinates_source: centroid of kept spots (planning point, provisional); re-centre when spot pins are resolved
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage region page "Yarra Valley" (with Healesville, Yarra Glen, Lilydale); Visit Yarra Valley tourism brand; wine region.
new_destinations.reason: 15 kept spots. Warburton and the Upper Yarra go to Yarra Ranges National Park (gateway to Donna Buang); Healesville Sanctuary and the wineries stay here.

new_destinations.name: Yarra Ranges National Park
new_destinations.coordinates_source: centroid of kept spots (planning point, provisional); re-centre when spot pins are resolved
new_destinations.name_evidence: Wikivoyage page "Yarra Ranges National Park"; Visit Yarra Valley walking pages (Donna Buang, Marysville, Lake Mountain); Parks Victoria national park.
new_destinations.reason: 13 kept spots. The park candidate itself is realised as this destination, not as a spot of itself. Marysville and Warburton are its gateway towns. Overlap with Yarra Valley checked with the prescreen tool.

spots.name: Puffing Billy Railway
spots.bio: Heritage steam railway from Belgrave through Emerald and Lakeside to Gembrook, with open carriages.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 30156 page views

spots.name: Dandenong Ranges National Park
spots.bio: National park in four parts across the ranges, with picnic grounds and walking tracks.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Understand/See anchors the ranges around this park; picnic grounds, walking tracks.
spots.skeptic_objection: Fragmented park; its walks and gardens are separate candidates, so it may be a duplicate.

spots.name: Sherbrooke Forest
spots.bio: Forest of tall mountain ash on the ranges' southern slopes, with walking tracks near Sherbrooke and Belgrave.
spots.reason: kept; Wikivoyage names Sherbrooke Forest as the forest behind Belgrave; well-known lyrebird walks, a second-tier nature stop. Parks Victoria page unreachable (not evidence against).
spots.skeptic_objection: Well known bushland in the Dandenongs; but part of the Dandenong Ranges National Park.

spots.name: William Ricketts Sanctuary
spots.bio: Bush garden on Mount Dandenong Tourist Road with the sculptor William Ricketts' clay figures among ferns.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage See listing; free sculpture sanctuary, daily, about an hour.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source; Wikivoyage flags a dead link and fire-ban closures.

spots.name: National Rhododendron Gardens
spots.bio: Public gardens of rhododendrons and azaleas at Olinda, open daily.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage See; public gardens open daily.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source, seasonal bloom peak; spring crowds are not year-round.

spots.name: Mount Dandenong
spots.bio: Summit lookout at 633 m, the highest point of the ranges, with a view across Melbourne.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage names the summit scenic lookout over Melbourne; road-accessible.
spots.skeptic_objection: Quick viewpoint stop, could be part of the Dandenong Ranges National Park spot.

spots.name: Olinda
spots.bio: Village on Mount Dandenong Tourist Road with gardens, tea rooms and views, a base for the ranges' gardens.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 6414 page views

spots.name: Sassafras
spots.bio: Forest village in the ranges known for its tea rooms and bush setting.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 5159 page views

spots.name: Belgrave
spots.bio: Town at the end of the Belgrave train line and the start of the Puffing Billy railway.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 8381 page views

spots.name: Kokoda Memorial Track
spots.bio: Steep 1000-step staircase with historical plaques at Upper Ferntree Gully.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage See listing plus Yarra Valley tourism; 1000-step walk with plaques, 1+ hr.
spots.skeptic_objection: Short urban-edge staircase; overlaps Ferntree Gully National Park walks.

spots.name: Cloudehill Gardens
spots.bio: Garden of themed garden rooms at Olinda, known for its flowers.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: Yarra Valley tourism board names this renowned garden; a garden visit is over half an hour.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source, paid private garden.

spots.name: Alfred Nicholas Memorial Gardens
spots.bio: Historic gardens of the Burnham Beeches estate near Olinda, with a lake and extensive water features.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: tourism board walking listing; historic public gardens with lake and water features.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source, zero page views.

spots.name: Emerald Lake Park
spots.bio: Parkland around Lake Treganowan with walking trails, paddleboats and the Puffing Billy Lakeside station.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: two counted sources (Wikivoyage, tourism board); lake, trails, paddleboats.
spots.skeptic_objection: Local recreation park beside a town.

spots.name: Trees Adventure Glen Harrow Park
spots.bio: Tree-top ropes and zipline course among the trees in Belgrave.
spots.reason: kept; Wikivoyage Dandenong Ranges lists the ropes and zipline park; a permanent paid activity venue of hours.
spots.skeptic_objection: Commercial adventure operator; one source.

spots.name: Lysterfield Lake Park
spots.bio: Regional park around Lysterfield Lake with walking, cycling and picnic areas on Melbourne's eastern edge.
spots.reason: Narrow edge of the Dandenong base: Belgrave and the ranges are its nearest base, inside the 35 km span. Melbourne region only reviewed it as "Lysterfield Park" and did not keep it.
spots.skeptic_objection: Walking and cycling park for locals; may be a suburban park.

spots.name: Healesville Sanctuary
spots.bio: Zoos Victoria wildlife sanctuary with native animals and a breeding program, 4 km south of Healesville.
spots.reason: kept; 3 counted sources, 6910 page views

spots.name: Healesville
spots.bio: Town at the eastern end of the Yarra Valley with galleries, cafes and the rail trail, near the sanctuary.
spots.reason: kept; 3 counted sources, 12058 page views

spots.name: Domaine Chandon
spots.bio: Sparkling wine producer at Coldstream with tastings and a restaurant.
spots.reason: kept; Well-known sparkling winery with tastings, named by Wikivoyage; winery is a recognised visitor draw.
spots.skeptic_objection: Famous winery visitors go to; but a venue and the wine region is the draw.

spots.name: Yering Station
spots.bio: Historic winery and cellar door near Yarra Glen, one of the oldest vineyards in the valley.
spots.reason: kept; Victoria's oldest vineyard with historic buildings, cellar door and restaurant, a headline Yarra Valley winery in every guide. Wikivoyage page did not list it; guidebook-level knowledge, source not opened.
spots.skeptic_objection: Heritage winery known to guides; but a cellar door/restaurant.

spots.name: TarraWarra Museum of Art
spots.bio: Art museum of early Australian modernist and contemporary work, overlooking the vineyards.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 1251 page views

spots.name: Yarra Glen
spots.bio: Town in the heart of the Yarra Valley wine district with cafes and galleries.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 3686 page views

spots.name: Four Pillars Gin Distillery
spots.bio: Gin distillery in Healesville offering tastings and tours.
spots.reason: kept; Two Wikivoyage mentions; distillery tastings and tours are a recognised attraction like a brewery tour.
spots.skeptic_objection: A recognised distillery draw; but a venue/shop.

spots.name: Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail
spots.bio: 40 km walking and cycling trail on a former railway from Lilydale through the valley to Warburton.
spots.reason: kept; 3 counted sources, 2904 page views

spots.name: Coombe Yarra Valley Melba's Garden Walk
spots.bio: Seven acres of century-old gardens to walk through, near Dixons Creek.
spots.reason: kept; Century-old Melba estate gardens open to visitors, tourism-board listed; a garden walk is a half-hour-plus visit.
spots.skeptic_objection: Garden with history; but also a winery property.

spots.name: Yarra Valley Railway
spots.bio: Tourist railway running from Healesville on weekends and public holidays.
spots.reason: kept; Wikivoyage names the heritage railway at Healesville; the ride is the attraction, a permanent venue (runs weekends and holidays).
spots.skeptic_objection: Ride is the attraction with no distinct far end; but limited operating days.

spots.name: Gulf Station Historic Farm
spots.bio: Restored 19th-century working farm near Yarra Glen showing how a family lived on the land.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: tourism board arts-culture listing; restored working farm open to the public (National Trust).
spots.skeptic_objection: One source; open only on certain days.

spots.name: Maroondah Reservoir Park
spots.bio: Reservoir park east of Healesville with a picnic area and a walk.
spots.reason: kept; Wikivoyage names it, 5 km east of Healesville; reservoir park with picnic area, walks and lookout.
spots.skeptic_objection: Named in Wikivoyage Do; but a plain picnic reserve.

spots.name: Badger Weir
spots.bio: Weir and walking area near Healesville with forest walks to Coranderrk and the Slip tracks.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: two counted sources; forest walk and picnic area.
spots.skeptic_objection: Local picnic reserve; Wikivoyage entry has no description.

spots.name: Wirrawilla Rainforest Walk
spots.bio: Easy circuit walk through temperate rainforest in Toolangi State Forest.
spots.reason: kept; Visit Yarra Valley calls it an easy short rainforest circuit in Toolangi State Forest; a named walk.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source, short walk, similar to other rainforest walks.

spots.name: Lilydale
spots.bio: Town at the western gateway to the valley and the start of the Lilydale to Warburton Rail Trail.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 12823 page views

spots.name: Mount Donna Buang
spots.bio: Mountain with a 21 m lookout tower at 1,245 m, with views to the Dandenongs and Cathedral Range.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 9657 page views

spots.name: Donna Buang Rainforest Gallery and Skywalk
spots.bio: Boardwalk loop through cool temperate rainforest near Warburton, with a skywalk 15 m above the ground.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1+2: two Wikivoyage pages name it; a boardwalk and platform 15 m above the rainforest, a half-hour+ visit.
spots.skeptic_objection: Part of Yarra Ranges National Park, which may be listed separately.

spots.name: Lake Mountain
spots.bio: Mountain resort above Marysville with cross-country skiing in winter and summit walks in summer.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 4813 page views High Country region also lists it: dedupe at merge.

spots.name: Marysville
spots.bio: Mountain town on the ranges' eastern edge, base for Steavenson Falls, Lake Mountain and Lady Talbot Drive.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 14745 page views

spots.name: Steavenson Falls
spots.bio: One of Victoria's tallest waterfalls, reached on a walk from Marysville.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1: Visit Yarra Valley calls it one of Victoria's tallest waterfalls; Marysville's headline sight, floodlit and walkable.
spots.skeptic_objection: Single counted source.

spots.name: Warburton
spots.bio: Upper Yarra town and gateway to Mount Donna Buang, the rail trail and rainforest walks.
spots.reason: kept; 2 counted sources, 16691 page views

spots.name: Black Spur
spots.bio: Scenic drive through tall ash forest between Healesville and Narbethong.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1: Wikivoyage Yarra Valley features Black Spur Forest as its banner image; scenic forest drive with tall ash trees, a known second-tier stop.
spots.skeptic_objection: A drive, and a roadside forest stop; not a place to linger.

spots.name: Keppel Falls
spots.bio: Long cascade in the Taggerty River headwaters, reached on a walk from Lady Talbot Drive.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1: two counted sources (Wikivoyage, Visit Yarra Valley); waterfall reached by walk from Lady Talbot Drive.
spots.skeptic_objection: Wikivoyage gives no description; may be part of Lady Talbot Drive.

spots.name: Cathedral Range State Park
spots.bio: State park of jagged ridges and hiking, with the Jawbone car park as a main starting point.
spots.reason: kept; Rule 1: Visit Yarra Valley calls it some of the best hiking in the state; jagged ridges, a state park with Wikipedia article. High Country region also lists it: dedupe at merge.
spots.skeptic_objection: Single counted source and park is on the region's edge.

spots.name: South Jawbone Peak
spots.bio: Summit reached on a 3.5 km return hike from the Jawbone car park in Cathedral Range State Park.
spots.reason: kept; Visit Yarra Valley names the 3.5 km summit hike; a named peak walk.
spots.skeptic_objection: Part of Cathedral Range State Park; one source.

spots.name: Beeches Rainforest Walk
spots.bio: Short walk through cool temperate rainforest on Lady Talbot Drive near Marysville.
spots.reason: kept; Wikivoyage lists a short rainforest walk off Lady Talbot Drive; a named walk worth 30+ min.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source and a short walk; near-duplicate of the drive's other stops.

spots.name: Ada Tree
spots.bio: Giant mountain ash over 300 years old in the Yarra State Forest, reached by a short walk.
spots.reason: kept; Giant mountain ash after a short walk in Yarra Ranges forest, named by Visit Yarra Valley; a distinct natural landmark guides single out. Visit Yarra Valley page not re-opened; earlier counted source accepted.
spots.skeptic_objection: A named natural landmark; but far in State Forest, a short stop.

spots.name: O'Shannassy Aqueduct Trail
spots.bio: 30 km walking and cycling trail along the historic aqueduct above the Upper Yarra Valley.
spots.reason: kept; Visit Yarra Valley describes a 30 km walking and cycling trail along a historic aqueduct; a promoted trail.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source; a long linear trail with no single point.

spots.name: Kinglake National Park
spots.bio: National park on the Great Dividing Range slopes near Kinglake, with waterfall walks and the Andrew Hill summit.
spots.reason: Standalone: only three kept places (park, Masons Falls, Wombelano Falls), so no destination. 37 km from Yarra Valley centre, reached from the Whittlesea/Melbourne side and outside the valley span (~21 km).

spots.name: Masons Falls
spots.bio: Waterfall in Kinglake National Park reached by a 700 m walk from Masons Falls Picnic Area.
spots.reason: Standalone: inside Kinglake National Park (which is itself standalone, three places). 37 km from Yarra Valley centre, outside its span.
spots.skeptic_objection: Part of Kinglake NP as a larger spot; one source.

spots.name: Wombelano Falls
spots.bio: Hidden waterfall just north of Kinglake, reached by a short easy walk.
spots.reason: Standalone: just north of Kinglake, outside every destination span; same cluster as Kinglake National Park.
spots.skeptic_objection: One source, small falls.

spots.name: Lake Eildon National Park
spots.bio: National park around Lake Eildon's shore with boating, camping and walking.
spots.reason: Standalone: ~50 km from Yarra Ranges National Park centre, reached from Eildon/Yea. High Country region also lists it: dedupe at merge.
spots.skeptic_objection: Wikipedia only; park largely water-based and may be handled with Eildon.

spots.name: Montsalvat
spots.bio: Artists' colony in Eltham from the 1930s, with galleries and a hall open to visitors.
spots.reason: Standalone: Eltham is Melbourne's north-eastern edge, 28 km from Yarra Valley centre and outside its span; 23 km from Dandenong Ranges but reached from Melbourne, not that base. A Melbourne destination, if one is created, may adopt it.
spots.skeptic_objection: One counted source; includes a restaurant and event venue.

review_list.name: Yarra Ranges Regional Museum
review_list.case: For: open museum in a purpose-built Lilydale building, tourism-board listed. Against: one source, a regional museum, short visit.

review_list.name: Mont De Lancey Historic Homestead
review_list.case: For: historic homestead open to public with cafe, tourism-board listed. Against: one source, small local heritage site.

review_list.name: Peninsula Tunnels
review_list.case: For: gold-era river diversion tunnels, walkable heritage site near Warburton. Against: one source, niche, short visit.

neighbour_notes: Lake Mountain, Cathedral Range State Park and Lake Eildon National Park are also kept by region vic-high-country: placed here, merge step must dedupe (one id each).
Melbourne region owns Dandenong Market and Yarra Bend Park only; it reviewed Lysterfield Park (not kept), so Lysterfield Lake Park is placed here under Dandenong Ranges.
Montsalvat (Eltham) is left standalone; if the Melbourne run creates a Melbourne destination covering Eltham, it may become its spot.
Kept candidate "Yarra Ranges National Park" is the destination yarra-ranges-national-park itself, not a spot.

standalone_within_40km_of_new_destinatio.why_not_a_spot: outside valley span (~21 km); reached from Whittlesea/Melbourne side, and only three Kinglake places
Eltham is a Melbourne suburb outside the valley span; also 23 km from Dandenong Ranges, reached from Melbourne
outside 75% of the 35 km span (~13 km)

coordinate_notes: Candidate coordinates are Wikipedia/Wikivoyage points or null. Null pins are unresolved; the pins stage runs resolve-pin.py for all.
